profile.campus: Forest City, Rutherford County, North Carolina (Meta's Forest City data center campus, Meta's second-ever data center after Prineville, Oregon)
profile.address: Solon David Smart Memorial Highway, Rutherford County, North Carolina, 28043
profile.reading:
This Meta data center building is one of four Meta structures that OpenStreetMap maps together at Meta's Forest City campus in Rutherford County, North Carolina, the company's second self-built data center campus after Prineville, Oregon. Beyond its approximate position within that four-building cluster, there is no public, operator-confirmed fact that distinguishes this specific building from its neighbors. Meta does not publish separate specifications, addresses, or capacity figures for individual Forest City buildings, so everything below describes the campus as a whole rather than this structure in isolation.

Facebook announced the original 300,000-square-foot building in November 2010, committing $450 million over five years and buying 150 acres of land on the site of a former manufacturing facility whose existing 44kV and 12.5kV power infrastructure and water capacity helped attract the project, according to Data Center Knowledge's contemporaneous reporting. Construction was expected to take about 18 months, putting the first building online around 2012. Facebook chose Forest City partly to give itself an East Coast counterpart to its West Coast data centers and to join Google and Apple, which had already built major facilities in the same part of western North Carolina. Facebook announced a second Forest City building in October 2011, and a third, roughly 480,000-square-foot building in October 2015, backed by more than $200 million in additional capital investment and a commitment to retain more than 125 full-time jobs, according to the Rutherford County Economic Development Commission. That 2015 expansion also included more than $575,000 in local school and nonprofit funding and a partnership to provide free Wi-Fi to students and families in the area.

Meta's own current fact sheet for the campus reports more than $750 million invested overall, a groundbreaking dated to 2010, roughly 275 operational jobs once complete, hundreds of peak skilled-trade construction workers, more than $5.9 million in direct funding to local schools and nonprofits, and a Meta-supported project adding 310 megawatts of new renewable energy generation in North Carolina. That renewable-energy figure describes a state-level generation commitment tied to Meta's North Carolina operations broadly rather than a confirmed on-site utility or IT-load capacity for the Forest City campus specifically, and Meta does not publish a campus-wide megawatt figure for the site's actual power draw. The fact sheet also states Meta's standard commitments to LEED Gold construction, 100 percent renewable electricity matching, and being water-positive by 2030.

Meta does not publish a specific street address, current total building count, or per-building square footage for individual Forest City structures. The address recorded for this facility is derived from reverse-geocoding its mapped coordinates rather than from an operator-published source, and should be treated as an approximate location rather than a confirmed mailing address. Rutherford County sits in the broader western North Carolina data center corridor that also includes Google's Lenoir campus and Apple's Maiden campus, a cluster regional economic-development groups such as the Rutherford County EDC have promoted as a hub for large technology capital investment tied to available industrial land and Duke Energy's regional transmission infrastructure.

reading.body:
Forest City is Meta's second self-built data center campus, opened in 2012 on the site of a former North Carolina manufacturing facility with inherited power infrastructure. Meta has invested more than $750 million across four buildings at the location and maintains more than 275 operational jobs there. Meta does not publish a combined power figure, IT-load capacity, or current total square footage for the Forest City campus, so its actual size relative to other AI data centers cannot be determined from operator disclosures.

The only power-related figure Meta has associated with Forest City is a $310 million renewable energy generation commitment across North Carolina broadly, which describes a state-level clean-energy project tied to Meta's North Carolina footprint generally rather than a confirmed utility draw or IT capacity for this specific campus. Historical announcements describe a 300,000-square-foot first building and a 480,000-square-foot third building, totaling roughly 780,000 square feet across those two structures alone, but Meta has never disclosed the size of the second and fourth buildings or a current campus total.

Forest City sits in the western North Carolina data center corridor alongside Google's Lenoir campus and Apple's Maiden campus, all supplied by Duke Energy's regional transmission infrastructure. North Carolina has 19 mapped data center facilities overall, but only five publish megawatt figures, and Meta does not disclose Forest City's power draw, making it impossible to rank the campus's actual capacity or its significance to state AI infrastructure from public data.
